goal: Provide secure, repeatable, and effective GitHub-based security evaluation for supported Filecoin ecosystem projects without representing incomplete evaluation as safety.

status_semantics.pending: Not started; dependencies may or may not be complete.
status_semantics.in_progress: Claimed as the single active task.
status_semantics.blocked: Work began but cannot continue without an external decision or state change.
status_semantics.done: Acceptance criteria and verification are complete.
status_semantics.cancelled: Intentionally removed from the active roadmap with rationale recorded in the decision map.

tasks.title: Establish navigable documentation foundation
tasks.objective: Give consumers, maintainers, and rollout operators tested paths into the platform.
acceptance_criteria: The root README routes all three audiences.
Consumer, maintainer, operator, architecture, and current-contract pages are indexed and link-checked.
verification: bash scripts/check-docs.sh

tasks.title: Create canonical machine-readable roadmap state
tasks.objective: Make roadmap order, dependencies, status, acceptance criteria, and verification queryable by people and automation.
acceptance_criteria: One JSON state file contains every implementation task in dependency order.
A checked-in command validates, queries, and deliberately updates task status.
verification: bash scripts/roadmap.sh validate
bash scripts/roadmap.sh next

tasks.title: Define execution trust tiers
tasks.objective: Classify every evaluation as inspection-only or code-executing and define its token, secret, network, runner, cache, and OIDC boundary.
acceptance_criteria: Every existing workflow is assigned to the Ecosystem Baseline or a named Privileged Analysis tier.
The baseline is specified as read-only, secretless, and non-executing on untrusted pull requests.
verification: A contract test compares workflow behavior with the recorded trust classification.

tasks.title: Enforce least privilege and safe checkout
tasks.objective: Give each workflow only its documented permissions and prevent checkout credentials from persisting.
acceptance_criteria: Every job has explicit permissions and every checkout sets persist-credentials to false.
OIDC, PR write, and security-event write permissions exist only in jobs that need them.
verification: A workflow-security test fails on implicit permissions, persisted credentials, or excessive authority.

tasks.title: Remove package lifecycle execution from inspection workflows
tasks.objective: Inspect manifests, lockfiles, licenses, and SBOM inputs without running consumer installation hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline dependency, license, and SBOM workflows do not run npm, pnpm, Cargo, Go, or other project hooks.
Build-dependent completeness is isolated behind explicit opt-in and reported as such.
verification: A malicious-install-hook fixture proves baseline jobs do not execute repository code.

tasks.title: Make scanner exit and gate semantics honest
tasks.objective: Prevent findings and operational failures from being hidden by unconditional advisory execution.
acceptance_criteria: Every scanner distinguishes finding thresholds from tool failure.
Every supported gate input is exposed and forwarded through the umbrella surface.
verification: Fixtures separately assert no findings, gated findings, tool error, and malformed output behavior.

tasks.title: Add completion status to existing evaluations
tasks.objective: Represent complete, incomplete, skipped, and error independently from finding severity.
acceptance_criteria: Each existing evaluation emits a machine-readable completion status.
AI refusal, truncation, missing secrets, event skips, and tool outages cannot appear as zero-findings completion.
verification: Contract fixtures cover all four completion statuses for scanner and AI surfaces.

tasks.title: Provide secretless secret scanning
tasks.objective: Run useful secret detection for organization repositories and fork pull requests without a required license secret.
acceptance_criteria: The default secret scanner works without repository or organization secrets.
PR-diff and scheduled full-history scopes are explicit and independently testable.
verification: Fork and full-history fixtures detect planted secrets with no configured secrets.

tasks.title: Add consumer GitHub Actions security evaluation
tasks.objective: Detect mutable references, excessive permissions, dangerous triggers, expression injection, persisted credentials, and OIDC exposure in consumer workflows.
acceptance_criteria: The baseline includes pinned workflow syntax and security analyzers.
High-confidence workflow supply-chain defects produce actionable locations and remediation.
verification: Fixtures cover mutable refs, pwn-request triggers, shell injection, and overbroad permissions.

tasks.title: Choose the cross-organization distribution model
tasks.objective: Confirm whether immutable public reusable workflows are sufficient for initial self-service delivery and define when a GitHub App becomes justified.
acceptance_criteria: The initial delivery mechanism, access assumptions, and escalation criteria are recorded.
The decision covers independent organizations, public/private repositories, forks, updates, and rollback.
verification: A sandbox consumer in another organization can install the selected delivery model.

tasks.title: Make consumer pins cover the complete execution graph
tasks.objective: Ensure one reviewed consumer SHA immutably selects nested workflows, actions, containers, prompts, rules, and third-party dependencies.
acceptance_criteria: No released execution path resolves mutable main, branch, floating tag, or unpinned container references.
Consumers can upgrade and roll back by changing one reviewed reference.
verification: A release-graph test recursively rejects mutable references and verifies all expected assets.

tasks.title: Prove fork-safe baseline behavior
tasks.objective: Give external contributions deterministic baseline evaluation without secrets or privileged triggers.
acceptance_criteria: Ordinary pull_request events from forks run every declared baseline evaluation or report an explicit skip.
No pull_request_target path checks out or executes untrusted fork content.
verification: An end-to-end fork fixture probes token, secret, checkout, cache, and OIDC boundaries.

tasks.title: Enforce the G0 trustworthy-foundation gate
tasks.objective: Turn every G0 trust claim into a required regression test and block release when one fails.
acceptance_criteria: Permissions, no-execution, gate semantics, completion, fork behavior, and release integrity are CI requirements.
The current consumer examples pass the same checks as released surfaces.
verification: The G0 suite passes cleanly and each control has a demonstrated failing fixture.

tasks.title: Finalize the Evaluation Result contract
tasks.objective: Version one schema for tool identity, scope, completion, coverage, findings, suppressions, timing, and evidence.
acceptance_criteria: Completion, findings, and Merge Gate policy are separate fields with explicit semantics.
Schema evolution and unknown-field behavior are documented.
verification: Valid and invalid fixture results are checked against the schema.

tasks.title: Implement the scanner adapter contract
tasks.objective: Give every evaluation the same lifecycle for immutable invocation, raw evidence, normalization, and exit handling.
acceptance_criteria: One vertical scanner slice implements the entire adapter contract without tool-specific policy leakage.
Operational errors and malformed output cannot be normalized as clean findings.
verification: Adapter contract tests run against success, findings, timeout, crash, and malformed-output fixtures.

tasks.title: Aggregate one Evidence Bundle and profile conclusion
tasks.objective: Present humans and automation with one authoritative completion, findings, coverage, and policy surface.
acceptance_criteria: The pipeline emits a versioned JSON Evidence Bundle and readable job summary.
One stable required check evaluates completion and the consumer-selected Merge Gate.
verification: Aggregation fixtures cover mixed findings, skipped jobs, errors, suppressions, and duplicate evidence.

tasks.title: Release the secretless Ecosystem Baseline
tasks.objective: Combine workflow security, secret detection, recursive lockfile vulnerabilities, IaC, and conservative static analysis without executing project code.
acceptance_criteria: The baseline is useful for supported Go, Rust, JavaScript, Solidity, infrastructure, and monorepo repositories without secrets.
Unsupported or unavailable coverage is visible in the Evidence Bundle.
verification: Cross-language fixtures pass the baseline and detect planted high-confidence defects.

tasks.title: Split fast PR and deep scheduled evaluation lanes
tasks.objective: Keep pull-request feedback timely while retaining full-history and whole-repository coverage on trusted events.
acceptance_criteria: PR evaluation is change-aware and stays within a documented runtime budget.
Push and schedule evaluation covers full history or repository scope where required.
verification: Event-matrix tests assert the declared scope and completion status for each lane.

tasks.title: Finalize the supported Security Profile taxonomy
tasks.objective: Define required, optional, unsupported, and privileged evaluations for real Filecoin project classes.
acceptance_criteria: Go node, Rust/FVM actor, service, Solidity/FEVM, and infrastructure profiles have owners and coverage statements.
Consensus-critical and funds-moving projects have explicit human-review requirements.
verification: Representative repositories map to one or more profiles without an unreported component.

tasks.title: Implement profile detection and composition
tasks.objective: Select profiles from repository signals and compose them by path for monorepos without hiding ambiguity.
acceptance_criteria: Detection recognizes supported manifests, build files, infrastructure, and Filecoin-specific signals.
Ambiguous and unsupported components produce explicit coverage gaps rather than guesses.
verification: Repository-shape fixtures cover single-language, polyglot, nested, and ambiguous layouts.

tasks.title: Ship the Go node and service profile
tasks.objective: Add low-noise Go dependency reachability, static analysis, and a separately trusted build tier suitable for node and service repositories.
acceptance_criteria: The profile includes pinned govulncheck and appropriate CodeQL/static analysis with documented build requirements.
Fork-safe inspection and trusted build-dependent coverage remain separate.
verification: Go fixtures cover reachable/unreachable advisories, build failure, and representative node code.

tasks.title: Pass the G1 internal-alpha gate
tasks.objective: Prove the immutable baseline and one vertical profile can be adopted end to end by a new consumer.
acceptance_criteria: A sandbox consumer installs through the documented quickstart without source assistance.
Upgrade, rollback, findings, incomplete execution, and required-check behavior are exercised.
verification: A recorded sandbox run and acceptance checklist satisfy every G1 criterion.

tasks.title: Ship the Rust and FVM actor profile
tasks.objective: Add RustSec or OSV dependency analysis, dependency policy, no-build static analysis, and actor-aware controls.
acceptance_criteria: The profile covers advisories, licenses, sources, unsafe-code evidence, and supported static analysis.
Actor-specific limitations and trusted WASM/build analysis are explicit.
verification: Rust fixtures cover vulnerable crates, policy violations, unsafe usage, and actor code.

tasks.title: Ship the JavaScript and TypeScript service profile
tasks.objective: Turn the current strongest generic coverage into a deterministic service profile with no-install and trusted-build tiers.
acceptance_criteria: Semgrep, CodeQL, lockfile vulnerabilities, dependency review, and IaC defaults are versioned and tested.
npm and pnpm install hooks are never required for baseline coverage.
verification: Service fixtures cover vulnerable dependencies, injection, authentication, workflow, and IaC defects.

tasks.title: Ship the Solidity and FEVM profile
tasks.objective: Combine safe source inspection with an explicit trusted Foundry, Slither, fuzz, and invariant-testing tier.
acceptance_criteria: Slither configuration and compiler resolution are deterministic and path-aware.
Build, fuzz, and invariant execution has no secrets, persisted credentials, write token, or OIDC.
verification: FEVM fixtures cover standard Solidity defects and Filecoin-specific address, epoch, gas, and actor-call behavior.

tasks.title: Ship the infrastructure and container profile
tasks.objective: Evaluate IaC, Kubernetes, Dockerfiles, container images, and build provenance with deployable policy defaults.
acceptance_criteria: Source configuration and built-image evaluation are distinct trust tiers.
The profile reports misconfiguration, vulnerable image content, and missing or invalid provenance.
verification: Infrastructure fixtures cover Terraform, Kubernetes, Dockerfile, image, and provenance failures.

tasks.title: Support composed monorepo evaluation
tasks.objective: Run multiple profiles by path while preserving scope, deduplication, runtime limits, and a single repository conclusion.
acceptance_criteria: Each component has an explicit profile, path scope, completion status, and findings set.
Shared dependencies and findings are deduplicated without hiding component-specific impact.
verification: Polyglot monorepo fixtures exercise nested and overlapping project boundaries.

tasks.title: Convert Filecoin invariants into deterministic controls
tasks.objective: Move high-confidence consensus, actor, FEVM, node-liveness, RPC, and storage-provider checks from prompt guidance into testable rules and invariants.
acceptance_criteria: Each rule names its supported scope, failure scenario, severity, precision expectation, and owner.
Rules with unacceptable false positives remain advisory or are excluded from Merge Gates.
verification: Planted Filecoin defect fixtures measure recall and precision for every released rule.

tasks.title: Pass the multi-profile effectiveness gate
tasks.objective: Demonstrate safety, portability, completion reliability, useful detection, and acceptable noise across representative profiles.
acceptance_criteria: Go, Rust, service, Solidity, infrastructure, and monorepo fixtures meet declared recall, precision, runtime, and completion thresholds.
Upgrade, rollback, outage, malformed evidence, and suppression behavior are exercised.
verification: The versioned corpus produces a published G2 effectiveness report.

tasks.title: Choose safe privileged-analysis behavior for forks
tasks.objective: Define no-checkout, maintainer-approved, or app-mediated paths for analyses requiring secrets or write access.
acceptance_criteria: Every fork receives evaluated, skipped, pending, or incomplete status for each privileged analysis.
No design combines untrusted checkout or execution with secrets or write authority.
verification: Fork threat-model fixtures demonstrate the selected approval and token flow.

tasks.title: Make AI review bounded and completion-aware
tasks.objective: Partition large diffs, collect deterministic context, handle refusal and truncation honestly, and emit the Evaluation Result contract.
acceptance_criteria: Large changes are partitioned with a coverage manifest instead of byte-truncated mid-diff.
Refusal, partial output, missing secrets, invalid schema, and provider outage produce explicit non-complete status.
verification: AI fixtures cover prompt injection, truncation, refusal, malformed output, and provider failure.

tasks.title: Validate AI findings, privacy, and cost
tasks.objective: Measure AI review as attributable evidence rather than treating model output or availability as correctness.
acceptance_criteria: Findings have independent validation or are clearly marked unvalidated with confidence.
Data handling, retention, model changes, per-run limits, and cost budgets are documented and enforced.
verification: The Filecoin corpus publishes AI recall, precision, completion, latency, and cost results.

tasks.title: Establish ownership and vulnerability response
tasks.objective: Protect the control repository with explicit owners, review rules, private reporting, support, and emergency response.
acceptance_criteria: CODEOWNERS covers workflows, actions, schemas, profiles, prompts, rules, and releases.
SECURITY, support, incident, and emergency revocation processes name accountable maintainers.
verification: A tabletop release-compromise and consumer-notification exercise completes successfully.

tasks.title: Automate signed releases, compatibility, and revocation
tasks.objective: Publish immutable, reviewable versions with changelogs, compatibility guarantees, dependency updates, rollback, and emergency revocation.
acceptance_criteria: Release artifacts and refs are signed or attested and generated only from protected reviewed commits.
Compatibility, deprecation, upgrade, rollback, and revocation policies are executable and documented.
verification: A release rehearsal verifies provenance, installation, upgrade, rollback, and revocation.

tasks.title: Generate reference documentation from released metadata
tasks.objective: Keep workflow inputs, outputs, permissions, secrets, profiles, schemas, and versions synchronized with implementation.
acceptance_criteria: Released contracts generate consumer reference tables and examples.
Documentation CI detects every metadata, example, and implementation disagreement.
verification: Regeneration is clean and an intentional contract mismatch fails CI.

tasks.title: Build profile selection and migration tooling
tasks.objective: Generate a minimal pinned consumer workflow and compatibility report without copying platform implementation.
acceptance_criteria: The tool detects profiles, explains ambiguity, emits minimal permissions, and records coverage gaps.
It supports install, upgrade, policy tightening, rollback, and visible time-bounded exceptions.
verification: Golden fixtures cover fresh installation and migrations from every supported prior release.

tasks.title: Pilot representative Filecoin projects
tasks.objective: Exercise self-service adoption across low-, medium-, and consensus-critical repositories in independent organizations.
acceptance_criteria: Pilot cohorts include every supported profile, forks, monorepos, and varied criticality.
Each pilot records installation effort, completion, findings, noise, runtime, remediation, upgrade, and rollback.
verification: Maintainers sign off on pilot reports and unresolved coverage gaps are assigned owners.

tasks.title: Operationalize staged Merge Gates and support
tasks.objective: Move projects from observation to critical-only and profile policy without surprise blocking or permanent exceptions.
acceptance_criteria: Gate stages, triage ownership, suppression expiry, escalation, and rollback are documented and exercised.
Consumer Engineers and Rollout Operators have named support and feedback channels.
verification: Pilot projects complete a simulated high finding, tool outage, exception expiry, and rollback.

tasks.title: Pass the public-v1 release gate
tasks.objective: Publish v1 only after trust, effectiveness, profiles, governance, migration, documentation, and support evidence is reviewed.
acceptance_criteria: Every G3 exit criterion has durable evidence and an accountable approver.
The public release is immutable, documented, supportable, upgradeable, and revocable.
verification: The signed v1 release checklist and clean-room consumer installation both pass.

tasks.title: Operate ecosystem health and effectiveness continuously
tasks.objective: Measure whether adoption improves security outcomes rather than merely increasing workflow count.
acceptance_criteria: Operators track adoption, version drift, completion, triage time, confirmed findings, false positives, remediation, runtime, and cost without collecting consumer source.
Profile owners review effectiveness and update or retire controls on a recurring schedule.
verification: A recurring G4 report identifies unhealthy consumers, stale profiles, and measured control changes.
